about: stone doctor's failure catalog: what each failure looks like, the words people use for it, its causes with priors, printer and material modifiers, the question that tells causes apart, the fix (cheapest and safest first) and the source. Priors and multipliers are stone's modeling assumptions, not measured rates.
assumption: prior, modifiers and answer multipliers are hand-set weights, checked only by evals/doctor

failures.name: Part came loose from the plate

looks_like.camera: the part is off its spot, tilted, moved or lying loose on the plate, often with loose strands under its edges
looks_like.part: the bottom is clean or only partly printed; first layers peeled off in one piece

causes.cause: Oil from fingers, dust or old glue on the plate

tells.ask: Wet the cold plate with a little water: does the water bead into drops, or spread as a thin film?
Has the plate gone several prints without a wash, or been touched with bare fingers?

fix: Wash the cold plate with warm water and plain dish soap (no lotion or oils), scrub, rinse, dry with a paper towel.
Do not touch the print area afterward; hold the plate by its edges.
Use the plate the slice expects and a thin glue stick layer if the maker suggests it for this filament.

causes.cause: First layer too far from the plate (leveling or Z offset)

tells.ask: Were the first-layer lines round and separate, instead of pressed flat into each other?
Was the printer moved, the plate swapped, or the firmware updated since it last printed well?

fix: Run the printer's own bed leveling and calibration before the next print.
Lower the Z offset in small steps (0.02 mm) until the first lines press flat into each other.
Clear any plastic off the nozzle tip first: a stuck bit makes homing read the bed wrong.

causes.cause: Bed too cold for the filament, or the slicer's plate or filament setting does not match

tells.ask: Do the slicer's filament and plate settings match the filament loaded and the plate on the printer?

fix: Pick the printer maker's preset for this exact filament and the plate type on the printer.
Use the bed temperature on the filament's label (stone refs <material> lists it).

causes.cause: Too little of the part touches the plate

tells.ask: Does the part touch the plate with only a small area, thin edges or points?

fix: Add a brim (5 to 8 mm) or mouse ears at the corners.
Turn the part so its largest flat face is on the plate.

causes.cause: Cold or drafty room cools the part and the plate

tells.ask: Is the room cold (below about 15 C) or drafty?

fix: Close the door or lid, or move the printer out of the draft.
Below about 15 C, raise the bed 10 C (Creality's advice).

differentials.tell_apart: a first-layer problem leaves the part stuck but with gaps or ridges
warping lifts only the corners while the middle stays stuck; a loose part came off whole
a loose part often ends up stuck on the nozzle; look for a lump around the heater block
a tall thin part that fell over still has its first layers stuck to the plate

looks_like.camera: the corners or ends of the part curl up off the plate while the middle stays down
looks_like.part: the bottom is bowed or the corners are raised; the base is not flat

causes.cause: The filament shrinks as it cools (ABS, ASA, PC, nylon most)

tells.ask: Is the part ABS, ASA, PC or nylon printed with the door open or no enclosure?

fix: Print it enclosed with the door closed and let the chamber warm first.
Add a brim of 5 to 10 mm.
Turn the part cooling fan down for this filament.

causes.cause: Oil from fingers, dust or old glue on the plate

tells.ask: Wet the cold plate with a little water: does the water bead into drops, or spread as a thin film?
Has the plate gone several prints without a wash, or been touched with bare fingers?

fix: Wash the cold plate with warm water and plain dish soap (no lotion or oils), scrub, rinse, dry with a paper towel.
Do not touch the print area afterward; hold the plate by its edges.
Use the plate the slice expects and a thin glue stick layer if the maker suggests it for this filament.

causes.cause: Cold or drafty room, or a part fan blowing hard on the base

tells.ask: Is the room cold (below about 15 C) or drafty?

fix: Close the door or move the printer away from drafts.
Raise the bed to the top of the filament's range.

causes.cause: A long part with sharp corners pulls hardest at its ends

tells.ask: Does the part touch the plate with only a small area, thin edges or points?

fix: Round the corners or add mouse ears.
Add a brim.
Split a long flat part or print it at an angle.

differentials.tell_apart: bed adhesion means the whole part came off; warping keeps the middle stuck
cracks split the walls between layers higher up; warping lifts the base
elephant foot bulges out at the base; warping bends it up

looks_like.camera: a tangle of loose filament (a bird nest) where the part should be, often around the nozzle
looks_like.part: the part is missing, broken off, or ends in a mess of strands

causes.cause: The part came loose and the printer kept going (see bed_adhesion)

tells.ask: Is the part, or its bottom layers, still stuck to the plate under the mess?

fix: Fix the adhesion first: stone doctor "part came off the bed" walks it.
Clean the plate.

causes.cause: An overhang or support failed and later layers printed onto nothing

tells.ask: Did the part have overhangs or supports where the mess started?
Is the part, or its bottom layers, still stuck to the plate under the mess?

fix: Turn on supports, or tree supports with more contact, where the slice shows overhangs past 45 degrees.
Turn the part so the overhangs face up.

causes.cause: Extrusion stopped or thinned mid print, so the layers above had nothing to stand on

tells.ask: Does the extruder click or grind while it should be pushing filament?
Is the part, or its bottom layers, still stuck to the plate under the mess?

fix: Check for a clog or a tangled spool (stone doctor "nothing comes out").
Dry the filament if it pops.

causes.cause: The nozzle knocked a thin part or a curled edge over

tells.ask: Is the part much taller than its footprint is wide?

fix: Add a brim, slow down, and use Z hop on travel moves.

differentials.tell_apart: if the bottom of the part came off whole, it is bed adhesion; spaghetti is what followed
if the part is still stuck and the mess starts at an overhang, the supports failed
if little plastic came out at all, the nozzle clogged

failures.name: Blob of plastic around the nozzle (hotend clumping)

looks_like.camera: a lump of plastic stuck around the nozzle and heater block, sometimes with the part or strands hanging from it
looks_like.part: the part is usually loose or ruined; the hotend is encased

causes.cause: A part that came loose stuck to the nozzle, and new plastic kept piling on

tells.ask: Did the part come loose from the plate before the plastic built up on the nozzle?
Wet the cold plate with a little water: does the water bead into drops, or spread as a thin film?

fix: Clear the blob safely first (safety lines above).
Then fix the adhesion: clean the plate (steps below).

causes.cause: The filament loaded does not match the slicer's filament (wrong temperatures)

tells.ask: Do the slicer's filament and plate settings match the filament loaded and the plate on the printer?

fix: Slice with the preset for the filament that is loaded.

causes.cause: No silicone sock, so ooze and stray strands build up on the heater block

tells.ask: Is the silicone sock on the heater block missing or torn?

fix: Fit a new silicone sock for this hotend.
Wipe the nozzle before each print (the printer's wiper must be clean).

causes.cause: The first layer was too low, so the nozzle dug in and dragged plastic

tells.ask: Were the first-layer lines round and separate, instead of pressed flat into each other?

fix: Recalibrate the Z offset or run the printer's leveling.

differentials.tell_apart: the blob usually starts with a part that came loose; check the plate too
spaghetti is loose strands in the air; a blob is a solid lump on the hotend
a heater or thermistor error after a blob means its wires are damaged

safety: Heat the hotend to about 30 C above the print temperature (PLA: about 250 C) before you pull plastic off; work in heat-resistant gloves (Prusa, Bambu and Creality guides).
The thermistor and heater wires are probably inside the blob: pull gently and never yank.
If the printer shows MINTEMP, a heater or thermistor error, a wire is already broken: power off and use a hair dryer or heat gun with care instead of the heater.
Afterward inspect the thermistor and heater wires and the silicone sock; replace what is damaged.

looks_like.camera: thin hairs or wisps of plastic stretched between separate parts or features, like a spider web
looks_like.part: fine strings or hairs between towers, holes or separate pieces

causes.cause: Wet filament oozes and strings

tells.ask: Has the spool been out of a dry box or bag for weeks, or do you hear popping from the nozzle?

fix: Dry the spool (stone refs <material> gives the drying temperature).
Store it in a box with desiccant.

causes.cause: Nozzle too hot for the filament

tells.ask: Is the nozzle temperature at the high end of the filament's range?

fix: Lower the nozzle temperature 5 to 10 C at a time.

causes.cause: Retraction too short or off

tells.ask: Is retraction turned off, or shorter than the slicer's profile for this printer?

fix: Use the maker's retraction for this printer, or print a retraction test and pick the cleanest.

differentials.tell_apart: wet filament also pops and leaves a fuzzy surface
zits are dots on the wall; strings stretch across gaps

looks_like.camera: thin, gappy walls and sparse infill; layers do not touch
looks_like.part: gaps in walls, holes, weak spotty infill

causes.cause: Partial clog in the nozzle

tells.ask: Does the extruder click or grind while it should be pushing filament?

fix: Do a cold pull, or swap the nozzle (stone doctor "nothing comes out" covers it).

causes.cause: Printing faster than the hotend can melt

tells.ask: Was it printing fast (above about 150 mm/s) or with high acceleration?

fix: Slow down or cap the volumetric flow at the filament preset's value.

causes.cause: Wet filament or a spool that drags

tells.ask: Does the filament on the spool cross over itself or pull tight before it reaches the printer?
Has the spool been out of a dry box or bag for weeks, or do you hear popping from the nozzle?

fix: Check the spool turns freely and is not tangled.
Dry the filament.

causes.cause: Flow or extrusion multiplier set too low, or wrong filament diameter

tells.ask: Do the slicer's filament and plate settings match the filament loaded and the plate on the printer?

fix: Run the printer's flow calibration and use the filament's preset.

differentials.tell_apart: a full clog extrudes nothing at all
pillowing is holes only in the top surface
grinding leaves a chewed flat spot on the filament

looks_like.camera: fat, blobby walls and ridges of extra plastic on the top surface
looks_like.part: parts come out too big; surfaces look overflowing

causes.cause: Flow or extrusion multiplier too high

tells.ask: Do the slicer's filament and plate settings match the filament loaded and the plate on the printer?

fix: Run the printer's flow calibration; lower flow by 2 to 5 percent at a time.

causes.cause: The slicer's filament diameter or preset is wrong

tells.ask: Do the slicer's filament and plate settings match the filament loaded and the plate on the printer?

fix: Check the slicer uses 1.75 mm (or 2.85 mm) to match the spool.

causes.cause: Nozzle too hot, so plastic overflows

tells.ask: Is the nozzle temperature at the high end of the filament's range?

fix: Lower the nozzle temperature 5 C at a time.

differentials.tell_apart: elephant foot is only the bottom layers
zits are separate dots, not fat walls

failures.name: Clog: little or nothing comes out

looks_like.camera: the printer moves but lays down little or no plastic; the part stops growing
looks_like.part: the print stops at a height or never starts

causes.cause: Debris or burnt plastic in the nozzle

tells.ask: When you unload the filament, is its tip swollen into a bulb or mushroom shape?

fix: Heat up and push the filament by hand; do a cold pull.
Swap the nozzle if it stays blocked.

causes.cause: Heat creep softened filament above the melt zone

tells.ask: When you unload the filament, is its tip swollen into a bulb or mushroom shape?
Was the door or lid closed while printing PLA?

fix: Check the hotend (heatsink) fan spins whenever the hotend is hot.
Open the door for PLA.

causes.cause: The extruder cannot grip or push (tension, worn gear, tangle)

tells.ask: Does the extruder click or grind while it should be pushing filament?
Does the filament on the spool cross over itself or pull tight before it reaches the printer?

fix: Check the spool is not tangled and the extruder tension; clean the gear.

causes.cause: Nozzle too cold, or pressed against the plate on the first layer

tells.ask: Do the slicer's filament and plate settings match the filament loaded and the plate on the printer?

fix: Use the filament's nozzle temperature; recalibrate the Z offset.

differentials.tell_apart: heat creep works for a while and then stops; the unloaded tip has a bulb
grinding chews a flat spot in the filament
a partial clog still extrudes, just too little

safety: Clear a clog with the hotend hot and the printer still; keep fingers off the nozzle and heater block.

failures.name: Layer shift: the part jumped sideways

looks_like.camera: part of the print is offset sideways from the layers below, like a staircase
looks_like.part: a clean step in the walls where everything above moved over

causes.cause: The nozzle hit a curled edge or the part

tells.ask: Did the nozzle hit a curled edge or the part before the shift (a knock sound)?

fix: Turn on Z hop for travel; fix curling (fan, temperature).
Avoid crossing the part on travel.

causes.cause: Loose or worn belts, or a loose pulley

tells.ask: When you pluck the X and Y belts with the printer off, are they slack or uneven?

fix: Tension the belts the way the maker describes; tighten pulley set screws.

causes.cause: Speed or acceleration above what the motors can hold

tells.ask: Was it printing fast (above about 150 mm/s) or with high acceleration?

fix: Use the maker's speed and acceleration limits; lower acceleration first.

causes.cause: Motor drivers or motors overheating

tells.ask: Was the door or lid closed while printing PLA?

fix: Check the electronics fan; give the printer air.

differentials.tell_apart: z wobble is many small even waves; a shift is one clean step
if the whole part slid, it came loose; a shift keeps the base in place

failures.name: Elephant foot: the base bulges out

looks_like.camera: the bottom few layers flare out wider than the walls above
looks_like.part: a lip or bulge at the base; parts do not fit together

causes.cause: First layer pressed too hard (Z offset low)

tells.ask: Is the bulge only in the first few layers, with the rest of the walls straight?

fix: Raise the Z offset slightly.
Turn on elephant foot compensation (0.1 to 0.2 mm).

causes.cause: Bed too hot, so the bottom layers stay soft under the weight above

tells.ask: Is the nozzle temperature at the high end of the filament's range?

fix: Lower the bed 5 to 10 C toward the low end of the filament's range.

causes.cause: The slicer's elephant foot compensation is off

tells.ask: Do the slicer's filament and plate settings match the filament loaded and the plate on the printer?

fix: Set elephant foot compensation to about 0.15 mm.

differentials.tell_apart: a first-layer problem shows in the bottom surface itself
over-extrusion makes every layer fat, not just the base

failures.name: Z banding: even horizontal lines up the part

looks_like.camera: regular horizontal bands or ridges up the side, evenly spaced
looks_like.part: a repeating pattern of lines on every wall

causes.cause: Lead screw bent, dirty or coupled off-center

tells.ask: Do the lines repeat at an even spacing up the whole part?

fix: Clean and grease the Z lead screws (the maker's maintenance steps).

causes.cause: Bed or nozzle temperature swinging

tells.ask: Do the lines repeat at an even spacing up the whole part?

fix: Run PID tuning for the bed and hotend; keep the printer out of drafts.

causes.cause: Inconsistent extrusion (filament diameter, partial clog)

tells.ask: Does the extruder click or grind while it should be pushing filament?

fix: Use good filament; check for a partial clog.

differentials.tell_apart: a layer shift is one step; banding repeats
ringing is ripples after corners, sideways; banding runs horizontally around the part

looks_like.camera: layers coming apart, splits between layers, weak bonds
looks_like.part: the part breaks along a layer line or peels apart by hand

causes.cause: Nozzle too cold for the filament or the speed

tells.ask: Is the nozzle temperature at the high end of the filament's range?

fix: Raise the nozzle temperature 5 to 10 C; slow down.

causes.cause: Too much part cooling

tells.ask: Is the part cooling fan at full speed, or blowing on the part from one side only?

fix: Lower the part fan, most of all for ABS, ASA and PETG.

causes.cause: Too little plastic between layers

tells.ask: Does the extruder click or grind while it should be pushing filament?

fix: Check for a partial clog and run flow calibration.

causes.cause: Layer height too large for the nozzle (over about 80 percent of it)

tells.ask: Do the slicer's filament and plate settings match the filament loaded and the plate on the printer?

fix: Keep layer height at or below 0.28 mm on a 0.4 mm nozzle.

differentials.tell_apart: cracks from shrinkage show in ABS or ASA on their own while cooling; delamination is weak bonding
under-extrusion shows gaps in the walls too

looks_like.camera: ripples or echoes of edges and letters repeating on the wall after sharp corners
looks_like.part: wavy ghost images next to features

causes.cause: Speed or acceleration too high for the frame

tells.ask: Was it printing fast (above about 150 mm/s) or with high acceleration?

fix: Lower acceleration first, then speed for outer walls.

causes.cause: Input shaping not calibrated (or changed since the printer was moved)

tells.ask: Was the printer moved, the plate swapped, or the firmware updated since it last printed well?

fix: Run the printer's input shaping or resonance calibration.

causes.cause: Loose belts, frame or a wobbly table

tells.ask: When you pluck the X and Y belts with the printer off, are they slack or uneven?

fix: Tension belts; tighten frame screws; put the printer on a solid surface.

differentials.tell_apart: banding is horizontal and even; ringing follows corners

looks_like.camera: the underside of overhangs sags or curls upward, rough and stringy
looks_like.part: droopy, saggy or curled edges under overhangs

causes.cause: Not enough part cooling on the overhang

tells.ask: Is the part cooling fan at full speed, or blowing on the part from one side only?

fix: Raise the part fan for overhangs; slow down on overhang perimeters.

causes.cause: Overhang steeper than the filament can bridge without support

tells.ask: Did the part have overhangs or supports where the mess started?

fix: Add supports past about 45 to 50 degrees, or turn the part.

causes.cause: Nozzle too hot, so the plastic stays soft

tells.ask: Is the nozzle temperature at the high end of the filament's range?

fix: Lower the nozzle temperature 5 C.

differentials.tell_apart: bridging sags between two supports; overhangs hang off one side
if supports were there and fell, it is a support failure

looks_like.camera: strands sag or hang loose in the middle of a span between two supports
looks_like.part: droopy strands across a gap; the bottom of the bridge is messy

causes.cause: Not enough cooling on the bridge

tells.ask: Is the part cooling fan at full speed, or blowing on the part from one side only?

fix: Run the part fan at 100 percent for bridges.

causes.cause: Bridge speed or flow too high

tells.ask: Was it printing fast (above about 150 mm/s) or with high acceleration?

fix: Lower bridge flow to about 0.85 to 0.95; slow bridges.

causes.cause: The span is too long for the filament

tells.ask: Did the part have overhangs or supports where the mess started?

fix: Add a support under long spans or shorten them.

differentials.tell_apart: an overhang hangs off one side; a bridge spans between two

looks_like.camera: supports fell over, broke off or are missing, and the part above printed onto nothing
looks_like.part: messy or missing surface where supports should have held it

causes.cause: Supports too thin or with too small a base

tells.ask: Is the part much taller than its footprint is wide?

fix: Use a support brim or raft for tall supports; use stronger tree branches.

causes.cause: Supports came loose from the plate

tells.ask: Wet the cold plate with a little water: does the water bead into drops, or spread as a thin film?

fix: Wash the cold plate with warm water and plain dish soap (no lotion or oils), scrub, rinse, dry with a paper towel.

causes.cause: The nozzle knocked supports over

tells.ask: Did the nozzle hit a curled edge or the part before the shift (a knock sound)?

fix: Turn on Z hop; slow travel near supports.

differentials.tell_apart: spaghetti is what follows a support failure
if the supports held but are fused to the part, the interface is wrong

failures.name: Support interface wrong: fused or not holding the part

looks_like.camera: supports welded to the part, or a rough, drooping surface right above the supports
looks_like.part: supports will not come off, or the surface above them is messy

causes.cause: Top contact Z distance too small (fused) or too big (droops)

tells.ask: Is the gap between support and part (top Z distance) set to zero or below one layer?

fix: Set top Z distance to about one layer height (0.2 mm for 0.2 mm layers).
Use an interface pattern the slicer suggests.

causes.cause: Hot sticky filament (PETG) bonds to its own supports

tells.ask: Is the nozzle temperature at the high end of the filament's range?

fix: Raise the Z distance a little for PETG; use a different interface material if the printer has more than one.

causes.cause: Interface layers too dense

tells.ask: Do the slicer's filament and plate settings match the filament loaded and the plate on the printer?

fix: Lower interface density or layers.

differentials.tell_apart: if the supports fell or broke, it is a support failure

failures.name: First layer wrong (gaps, too squished, uneven)

looks_like.camera: the first layer has gaps between lines, or is squashed see-through, or differs across the plate
looks_like.part: the bottom surface shows gaps, ridges or rough areas

causes.cause: Z offset or first-layer height wrong

tells.ask: Were the first-layer lines round and separate, instead of pressed flat into each other?

fix: Run the printer's calibration, then adjust the Z offset in 0.02 mm steps.

causes.cause: Bed mesh out of date, or the bed is not flat

tells.ask: Was the printer moved, the plate swapped, or the firmware updated since it last printed well?

fix: Run a full bed leveling (mesh); check the plate sits flat with nothing under it.

causes.cause: Dirty plate makes lines pull up

tells.ask: Wet the cold plate with a little water: does the water bead into drops, or spread as a thin film?

fix: Wash the cold plate with warm water and plain dish soap (no lotion or oils), scrub, rinse, dry with a paper towel.
Do not touch the print area afterward; hold the plate by its edges.
Use the plate the slice expects and a thin glue stick layer if the maker suggests it for this filament.

differentials.tell_apart: if the part came off, start with bed adhesion
a squished first layer can also flare the base out

failures.name: Zits and blobs on the walls

looks_like.camera: small bumps or pimples scattered on the outer wall
looks_like.part: random dots and blobs on the surface

causes.cause: Retraction and travel settings leave ooze where the nozzle stops

tells.ask: Is retraction turned off, or shorter than the slicer's profile for this printer?

fix: Turn on wipe and adjust retraction; use a seam position that hides the starts.

causes.cause: Wet filament spits

tells.ask: Has the spool been out of a dry box or bag for weeks, or do you hear popping from the nozzle?

fix: Dry the filament.

causes.cause: Nozzle too hot

tells.ask: Is the nozzle temperature at the high end of the filament's range?

fix: Lower the nozzle temperature 5 C.

differentials.tell_apart: a seam is one line in the same place; zits are scattered
wet filament also pops and looks fuzzy

looks_like.camera: a vertical line or scar running up one side where every layer starts
looks_like.part: one line of bumps or a groove up the wall

causes.cause: The seam sits on a visible face

tells.ask: Is the seam set to aligned or rear in the slicer?

fix: Set the seam to rear or paint it into a corner.

causes.cause: Pressure advance or retraction not tuned

tells.ask: Is retraction turned off, or shorter than the slicer's profile for this printer?

fix: Run the printer's pressure advance or linear advance calibration.

differentials.tell_apart: zits are scattered; a seam lines up

looks_like.camera: rough fuzzy or bubbly surface; steam or popping while it prints
looks_like.part: fuzzy, bubbly, rough walls with strings

causes.cause: The filament absorbed water from the air

tells.ask: Has the spool been out of a dry box or bag for weeks, or do you hear popping from the nozzle?

fix: Dry the spool at the maker's temperature (stone refs <material>).
Keep it in a sealed box with desiccant.

causes.cause: Nozzle too hot (boils additives)

tells.ask: Is the nozzle temperature at the high end of the filament's range?

fix: Lower the nozzle temperature.

differentials.tell_apart: strings alone, with no popping, may only be retraction
zits come from ooze at stops

failures.name: Heat creep: extrusion fades after a while

looks_like.camera: the print goes fine, then gets thinner and stops partway up
looks_like.part: the part stops at some height; the walls thin out before it

causes.cause: PLA in a closed, warm enclosure

tells.ask: Was the door or lid closed while printing PLA?

fix: Open the door or lid for PLA.
Check the chamber is not above about 35 C.

causes.cause: Hotend heatsink fan weak, dirty or stopped

tells.ask: When you unload the filament, is its tip swollen into a bulb or mushroom shape?

fix: Clean the hotend fan and check it spins when the hotend is hot.

causes.cause: Long retraction pulls soft plastic up into the cold zone

tells.ask: Is retraction turned off, or shorter than the slicer's profile for this printer?

fix: Use the maker's retraction length for this printer.

differentials.tell_apart: a clog from debris blocks from the start; heat creep builds over time

looks_like.camera: the extruder clicks or grinds; filament has a chewed spot; plastic dust at the gears
looks_like.part: under-extruded or stopped print

causes.cause: The nozzle is partly blocked, so the gear chews in place

tells.ask: When you unload the filament, is its tip swollen into a bulb or mushroom shape?

fix: Clear the nozzle first (cold pull), then check the gear.

causes.cause: Wrong extruder tension, or a tangled spool

tells.ask: Does the filament on the spool cross over itself or pull tight before it reaches the printer?

fix: Untangle the spool; set the extruder tension the way the maker says.

causes.cause: Brittle (old or wet) filament snaps in the path

tells.ask: Has the spool been out of a dry box or bag for weeks, or do you hear popping from the nozzle?

fix: Dry it, or replace a brittle spool.

differentials.tell_apart: a clog stops extrusion; grinding is the extruder failing to push
Under-extrusion alone: thin lines but the filament keeps moving; grinding: the gear chews a notch and the filament stops.
if a CFS, AMS or MMU reports the error, start there

looks_like.camera: a tall thin part lying on its side, broken off at the base
looks_like.part: snapped at a height, first layers still on the plate

causes.cause: Too tall for its footprint

tells.ask: Is the part much taller than its footprint is wide?

fix: Add a brim; print several copies together or add a support wall.

causes.cause: Nozzle hit it on a travel move

tells.ask: Did the nozzle hit a curled edge or the part before the shift (a knock sound)?

fix: Turn on Z hop; slow travel.

causes.cause: A bed slinger shakes tall parts

tells.ask: Was it printing fast (above about 150 mm/s) or with high acceleration?

fix: Lower Y acceleration; add a brim.

differentials.tell_apart: if the base came off too, it is adhesion
a toppled part can turn into spaghetti

looks_like.camera: cracks running along layer lines, often at corners or higher up
looks_like.part: horizontal cracks between layers that open as the part cools

causes.cause: The chamber is too cold for the filament

tells.ask: Is the part ABS, ASA, PC or nylon printed with the door open or no enclosure?

fix: Print enclosed with the door shut; let the chamber warm before starting.

causes.cause: Part fan too high for the filament

tells.ask: Is the part cooling fan at full speed, or blowing on the part from one side only?

fix: Lower the part fan to 0 to 20 percent for ABS and ASA.

causes.cause: Nozzle too cold for good layer bonding

tells.ask: Is the nozzle temperature at the high end of the filament's range?

fix: Raise the nozzle temperature 5 to 10 C.

differentials.tell_apart: PLA or PETG splitting is usually weak bonding, not shrinkage
warping lifts the base; cracks open higher up

failures.name: Pillowing: holes in the top surface

looks_like.camera: bumps and holes in the top surface where the infill shows through
looks_like.part: a lumpy top with gaps

causes.cause: Too few top layers or too sparse infill

tells.ask: Are there fewer than about 5 top layers, or under 15 percent infill?

fix: Use at least 5 top layers (about 1 mm) and 15 percent infill or more.

causes.cause: Not enough cooling over the infill

tells.ask: Is the part cooling fan at full speed, or blowing on the part from one side only?

fix: Raise the part fan for top layers.

causes.cause: Too little plastic on the top layers

tells.ask: Does the extruder click or grind while it should be pushing filament?

fix: Check flow and for a partial clog.

differentials.tell_apart: under-extrusion shows in the walls too
Poor bridging: strands sag across a gap in the walls; pillowing: the top skin over sparse infill sags between infill lines.

failures.name: CFS, AMS or MMU feed fault

looks_like.camera: the printer stops with a feed, load, cut or buffer error; filament stuck between the box and the head
looks_like.part: the print paused or stopped at a color change

causes.cause: Spool tangled or wound unevenly

tells.ask: Does the filament on the spool cross over itself or pull tight before it reaches the printer?

fix: Untangle or rewind the spool; check it turns freely.

causes.cause: Filament tip not cut cleanly (dull cutter or a bent tip)

tells.ask: Is the filament tip cut cleanly and straight when it unloads?

fix: Trim the tip straight before loading; check the cutter (Creality's K2 maintenance says inspect it every 5 rolls).

causes.cause: A broken piece of filament or a kinked tube in the path

tells.ask: Did the printer's screen show an error code or message?

fix: Follow the maker's jammed filament steps: remove the tube and clear the broken piece.

differentials.tell_apart: if the extruder clicks, the fault is at the head, not the box
a clog blocks the nozzle even with one spool

failures.name: Heater or thermistor error

looks_like.camera: the printer stopped with a thermal runaway, heater or temperature error on the screen
looks_like.part: the print stopped; the temperature reading jumps or fails

causes.cause: Thermistor loose or its wire damaged

tells.ask: Are the thermistor or heater wires at the hotend loose, pinched or broken?

fix: With the printer off and cool: check the thermistor is fully in the heater block and its wires are not pinched or broken.

causes.cause: A fan or a missing sock cools the heater block faster than it heats

tells.ask: Did the error happen while a fan turned on, or the hotend sock was off?

fix: Fit the silicone sock; check the part fan does not blow on the heater block.

causes.cause: Heater cartridge or its wiring failing

tells.ask: Are the thermistor or heater wires at the hotend loose, pinched or broken?

fix: Have the heater checked or replaced (the maker's hotend guide).

differentials.tell_apart: a recent blob often damages these wires

safety: Thermal errors are the firmware stopping a heater to prevent a fire: switch the printer off and let it cool before touching the hotend.
Do not restart the print until the cause is found.

looks_like.camera: something stone has no name for yet
looks_like.part: describe it in plain words: where on the part, what it looks like

causes.cause: Not in stone's catalog yet
fix: Describe the problem in more detail, or send a photo to stone doctor --image.

needs_heat: Heat the hotend to about 30 C above the print temperature (PLA: about 250 C) before you pull plastic off; work in heat-resistant gloves (Prusa, Bambu and Creality guides).
Clear a clog with the hotend hot and the printer still; keep fingers off the nozzle and heater block.
Heat up and push the filament by hand; do a cold pull.
Check the hotend (heatsink) fan spins whenever the hotend is hot.
Clean the hotend fan and check it spins when the hotend is hot.
Do a cold pull, or swap the nozzle (stone doctor "nothing comes out" covers it).
Clear the nozzle first (cold pull), then check the gear.
Run PID tuning for the bed and hotend; keep the printer out of drafts.
